title: Tenant cohort fairing and soft-respite orchestrator
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: During the 2024-09-18 regional surge incident we observed rapid tenant-level thrashing when circuit breakers and eviction policies ran independently: tenants repeatedly entered eviction, released, and were re-evicted within short windows causing wasted work and instability. This PR introduces a cohort-aware 'soft respite' orchestration layer that (1) groups tenants into short-lived cohorts for SLO relaxation windows, (2) provides a token-based respite lease extension to avoid rapid eviction/reinstate cycles, and (3) transitions the circuit breaker into a low-impact 'lull' state for cohorts meeting stability criteria instead of a full open. Approach: implement a RespiteOrchestrator in control plane that tracks ephemeral cohort membership (shuffle-once per 30s) and issues short respite leases (default 10s) using the existing lease API. Add heuristics to the circuit state machine to accept 'lull' transitions when cohort-level error rate is below a threshold and individual tenant token buckets indicate transient overloads. Feature gated behind runtime flag runtime.feature.respite_orchestrator (off by default). Rollout plan: behind feature flag -> unit and integration tests -> dogfood in canary region for 48h -> staged roll to US regions -> enable for EU with opt-in. Observability: new telemetry emitted under metric names respite.cohort_size, respite.granted_count, circuit.lull_entries, and debug logs emitted at TRACE only when runtime.debug.respite is enabled. Backwards compatibility: the orchestrator uses existing lease primitives and fallbacks to standard eviction machinery if the orchestrator fails. Reverts are supported by disabling the feature flag and removing orchestrator assignments from the control plane. Changes included: code (control plane orchestrator + circuit state machine updates), unit/integration tests, small additions to telemetry dashboard JSON, and an entry in ops/rollout.md. Risk: medium — logic touches eviction and circuit transitions; tests and dogfood period required. Linear/Jira: ENG-4921, SUP-7123. CI: initial run surfaced a flaky integration test around lease expiry (fixed by commit 3), full CI green after fix.

post_merge_notes: Merged to main via squash. Feature flag default remains off; ops runbook updated with steps to enable and monitor. Can be reverted by toggling runtime.feature.respite_orchestrator=false and allowing existing eviction flow to reclaim control. Telemetry panels are in telemetry/dashboards and will be added to the canary Grafana shortly.
release_notes: Add cohort-aware soft-respite orchestration to reduce tenant eviction/reinstate thrashing under transient overloads. Feature disabled by default; enable behind runtime.feature.respite_orchestrator. Monitor respite.cohort_size, respite.granted_count, and circuit.lull_entries.
incident_context: This change was motivated by incident SUP-7123 (2024-09-18) where short-cycle evictions amplified regional instability. The orchestrator aims to reduce rework and improve SLO stability during transient surges.
test_plan: Unit tests for orchestrator and state transitions; deterministic integration test that simulates cohort churn and lease expiry; canary run for 48h with detailed telemetry and alerting on eviction suppression > 5% of baseline.
notes_for_sre: When enabling in canary: set runtime.feature.respite_orchestrator=true and runtime.debug.respite=true for first 2 hours. Watch respite.granted_count and circuit.lull_entries; if queueing latency increases or error-rate drift > 0.5% for 5m, toggle off and capture logs with trace id prefix 'respite-run/'.
authors_reply_summary: Addressed reviewer concerns: added minResidenceTTL and jitter to prevent cohort oscillation, added telemetry for suppressed evictions, stabilized flaky test, and documented rollout. CI green and PR approved by all reviewers.
